newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE may expand Eurolira pit amid growing volume.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE may expand Eurolira pit amid growing volume.

text.p: As volume increases in Eurolira futures, LIFFE said on Friday it may expand the pit later in the year -- but pressure of space means any increase would be slight.

Eurolira futures trade on London's International Financial Futures and Options Exchange has risen sharply, with more than one million contracts traded last month, compared with just over 400,000 in March 1996. The first quarter of this year saw 3.3 million contracts traded, up 153 percent on first quarter 1996.
"We have great shortage of space and a huge reconfiguration in progress which we know is causing discomfort to our members," said Karin Forseke LIFFE's operating officer.
"There might be a tiny expansion in June, but we have just expanded the Euromark pit and primarily new space will be given to the mark products," she said.
Traders said the pit has had rather limited elbow-room over the last few weeks, amid speculation over Italian interest rates and concern over the issue of Italy's involvement in Albania.
Traders noted that the volume of trade in front month Eurolira futures often exceeded that in Euromarks.
By 0920 GMT, June, September and December 1997 Eurolira futures had traded a total of about 13,500 contracts, while the same three months in Euromarks had traded about 10,500.
